$comment: Authoritative attestation reference for the production publicai-gateway CVM. Fetched at runtime by the /proof page. composeHash was read back from the CVM's RTMR3 event log on 2026-08-29 and cross-checked against the Phala control-plane API; both report e247e0ca. Image digests are the linux/amd64 children of the cosign-signed proof-v21 index for sub2api (INDEX 4a950f0f) built by publish-tee-images run 33237496565 from commit e3f8f5c2e; the attestor image is deliberately left at its proof-v20 pin (INDEX cef1d03d) because deploy/attestor was not touched in this release, and repinning it would widen the attested surface for nothing. VERIFICATION SCOPE, stated plainly: composeHash, osImageHash, the image digests and the build commit were each read back from a live source, and composeHash was cross-checked against two independent ones. The cosign keyless signature was NOT verified locally for this release — the workflow performs the signing and its run succeeded, and anyone can verify certificate identity https://github.com/FiiLabs/sub2api/.github/workflows/publish-tee-images.yml@refs/heads/feat/two-sided-market plus the embedded githubWorkflowSha against the sourceCommit below, but this file does not claim it was done. This release adds supplier self-service re-authorization: when a supply account's upstream credential expires, the supplier can now swap a fresh token into the SAME account (POST /user/supply/accounts/:id/reauth/{start,complete}) instead of the previously only available path, disconnect-and-reconnect, which was irreversible, produced a new account id, restarted the observation window and dropped the supplier's own daily cap. The authorization is pinned to the account server-side — migration 237 adds supplier_oauth_sessions.account_id and the one-shot claim statement matches on it, so an onboarding session cannot repair an account and a repair session cannot mint a new one — and the incoming token must belong to the SAME upstream subscription. That identity gate is the reason an already-promoted account may stay live instead of re-entering observation; weakening it would turn an account id into a shell that any unvetted subscription could occupy while skipping the observation window. Two related fixes ship with it. First, an authentication-class probe failure (upstream 401) now marks the account errored, so the existing supplier-incident record and its notification email finally fire; previously such an account failed a probe every 15 minutes forever while its owner was told nothing. That classification lives in the supply lifecycle sweep rather than in the shared account-test path, which also serves the admin 'test connection' button for every first-party account. Second, re-authorization explicitly restores schedulable, closing a latent trap: SetError clears it, ClearError does not restore it, and the observation sweep only scans pending_review — so a single upstream 401 left a promoted supply account permanently unschedulable with no code path back. Earlier in this line: proof-v20 (supply concurrency 3->15), v19 (abuse detection, shipped disabled), v18 (take-offline copy), v17 (reference-source fix + first-screen 1332KB->118KB), v16/v15 (two-sided marketplace). osImageHash, appId and instanceId are unchanged; the deploy passed --no-dev-os explicitly, because phala deploy silently switches to a dev OS image when it detects a local SSH key and a dev OS would void the attestation. For the record, this rollout hit a Phala prod5 outage: the CVM stopped and then boot-looped for roughly forty minutes because dstack-prepare.sh could not reach gateway-rpc.dstack-pha-prod5.phala.network to register the CVM, and the kernel runs with panic=1, so the failed boot service rebooted the VM about 22 seconds in, repeatedly. Nothing in this release caused it, and rolling back would not have helped — registration happens before any application container starts. It recovered on its own once the gateway returned.
